claim_scope: V9 terminal families VAL-A/B/C/D (38 occurrences, 16 one-card fields) and its conditional measure prediction.

correction.actual_v9_test: No completed V9 measure test is present in the cited primary. The report records a predeclared conditional prediction: if the families are measures, adjacent overt numeral-like/ingredient-like cards should recur; one-card fields are adverse unless a stencil supplies quantity.
correction.what_16_one_card_fields_support: They challenge only a strict model requiring every measure occurrence to have an overt companion in the same field. They do not refute a unit-plus-number compound, an implicit argument, a stencil-supplied quantity axis, or a single-card abbreviation.
correction.unit_and_mapping: V9’s units are the four VAL terminal families and their field occurrences. GDT760’s unit is a separate census of 281 reader-exact amount forms with immediate neighbors; GDT804’s unit is 15 positional middle-form neighbors. No primary supplies a mapping from those amount forms/slots to VAL-A/B/C/D.
correction.nontransfer: Therefore GDT760/804 results cannot weaken or confirm V9’s measure prediction without an explicit cross-experiment mapping. GDT804’s failed CONTENT_PREP slot is local to its own amount/neighbor model.
correction.remaining_unknown: Whether any VAL family is a measure, whether quantity is overt or stencil-supplied, and whether one-card fields abbreviate a unit/quantity remain untested in V9. No universal non-significance or falsity claim follows.

evidence.quote:
The four largest committed terminal families are:

| neutral label | exact tuple prefix | total | one-card fields | after other cards | page distribution |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `VAL-A` | `bc4f1f5c006c74a4d26d` | 12 | 3 | 9 | f81v 4, f82r 1, f83r 7 |
| `VAL-B` | `7d25241b0e56c836372a` | 10 | 5 | 5 | f82r 5, f83r 5 |
| `VAL-C` | `de7321bface5628e35d6` | 8 | 5 | 3 | f82r 1, f83r 7 |
| `VAL-D` | `7db18b2f0fb7ed0fcfd3` | 8 | 3 | 5 | f81v 3, f83r 5 |

All 38 occurrences carry attached DY closure. The labels are deliberately not
ordered magnitudes and do not mean YES, NO, HOT, COLD, WATER, RESULT, or any
source-language word. `VAL-A` is the exact family whose surface realization is
represented by `shedy` in the current compact theory; that spelling is not an
expansion.

Three facts constrain the historical comparison.

1. Sixteen of the 38 occurrences are complete one-card fields. A model that
   requires an overt noun plus a following verbal formula must explain why the
   noun or verb can stand alone so often.

What it does not explain well: sixteen complete one-card fields and four
families that recur as interchangeable-looking field answers. Ordinary
ingredient or product abbreviations should normally retain more lexical
companions, while pure measure signs should be accompanied by numbers or
measured substances. This remains a plausible source layer, but is not the best
specific account of the 12/10/8/8 terminals.

The selected mechanism makes stronger predictions than a generic “technical
text” analogy.

1. In additional unsealed Biological material, the four values should remain
   enriched at field closure and in one-card fields, not diffuse through long
   open prose like ordinary nouns.
2. Repeated field-shape stencils should predict which subset of the value deck
   is licensed better than neighboring lexical cards do.
3. `VAL-A` should remain the most portable member; `VAL-B/C/D` should show
   stable page-, diagram-, or subtemplate-conditioned availability.
4. If the families are recipe products or efficacy formulae instead, they
   should correlate with larger record endings and preceding preparation
   sequences, not merely local field endings. The present page ecology favors
   the latter.
5. If they are route stations, independently annotated geometry should predict
   their identity or order. No such alignment currently exists.
6. If they are measures, adjacent overt numeral-like or ingredient-like cards
   should form a recurrent pairing. One-card fields are adverse evidence unless
   the quantity axis is independently supplied by the stencil.

Der Pass findet in 281 exakten Mengenformen 45 saubere unmittelbare Stoff- oder
Zubereitungskontakte. Eine Stelle besitzt auf beiden Seiten einen möglichen
Inhalt; deshalb entstehen 44 konkrete Mengen-Inhaltsphrasen aus 35
verschiedenen Ganzwörtern.

Die ursprünglich geplante Regel „Zutat steht links von der Menge“ ist falsch.
Global sind beide Seiten praktisch identisch: links 20/163 oder 12,2699 Prozent,
rechts 25/204 oder 12,2549 Prozent. Die Zeilenposition löst das scheinbare Chaos:

| Mengenposition | linke Inhaltsplätze | rechte Inhaltsplätze | Arbeitsrichtung |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Zeilenanfang | kein linker Platz | 14/72 | zuerst rechts lesen |
| Zeilenmitte | 19/140 | 11/132 | zuerst links lesen |
| Zeilenende | 1/23 | kein rechter Platz | kein automatischer Inhalt |

Das ist keine allgemeine Sprachwortstellung. Es ist eine unmittelbar
ausführbare Readerregel für genau diese Mengenformen.

## Die Mengenkarte bestätigt keinen einheitlichen Stoffslot

GDT804 findet 15 Nachbarn auf
der von GDT760 bevorzugten Seite (FIRST→rechts, MIDDLE→links), davon
14 zuvor offene Kandidaten.
Das sind **keine automatisch lizenzierten Inhaltsplätze**: Keine der fünfzehn
ausgewählten Mittelformseiten war in GDT760 bereits ein sauberer CONTENT_PREP-
Kontakt. In `f88r.10` steht zwar `cheol` auf der bevorzugten linken Seite, aber
GDT760s tatsächliche Inhaltslizenz gehört rechts zu `cheos`. Die offenen
Positionsnachbarn liegen im aggregierten Null bei 14.0056
(`p=0.648470305939`).
Damit fällt der behauptete einheitliche Stoffslot weg.
